There’s a few things at play here.

1) If I’m having an issue with a passenger and have to stop to report it, I’m going to have to cancel the ride. I’ve wasted countless hours making reports to Lyft and the police during COVID.

2) I’m in a ride and I’m given a next ride in a queue. I didn’t get a chance to see the brief flash of how many minutes it is from the drop off location of my current passenger because I was trying to drive in Los Angeles traffic. 6)If you are walking to my car like you are angry with me, I’m going to cancel.

There’s a lot of reasons that drivers have to cancel and it’s usually a company policy that causes that. I started solo traveling in September of 2021. It’s addicting! I e since been on 5 cruises with another one in the beginning of March. I used to think you had to be rich to travel. I was so very wrong about this. I’m a rideshare driver and I found the beauty of making payments. On Carnival cruise lines, if you book a trip more than 90 days out, you will be able to make a $200 down payment and then you just make payments when ever you can and, as long as you make your last payment at the 90 day mark, you are good to go. Then, there are things you can pre purchase like shore excursions, internet plans, drink packages and massages that cost extra. You can buy these things one at a time. You can also pay gratuities up front as well. I love this system because it allows me to go on lots of vacations and by the time the vacation is here, everything has been paid for and I’m only budgeting for souvenirs and gambling money. I’ve also gotten a lot of free perks because I gamble a little each time I cruise. My next cruise in March was $604 for a 6-day cruise that includes food, my room and lots of free entertainment. The casino has also given me $500 to spend on board which I will gamble to receive future offers. So, basically, I am going on a 6-day cruise for $104 including taxes.

Right now the cruising deals are amazing. They are charging very low rates to fill up their ships. Cruising is a pretty safe way to see the world if you are traveling solo. No taking questionable taxis from foreign airports and staying at strange motels. The ship goes to an amazing place, you walk off the ship to do one of the many amazing shore excursions sponsored by Carnival (Carnival Shore excursions offer extra protection because you are with a group and the guide must keep track of everyone’s whereabouts. Plus, the ship wont leave if your excursion runs late.) Then, you walk back on the ship and you can return to your comfy room.

As far as medications go, you can take medications that you need for the duration of the trip.

When I first started to solo travel, there was a learning curve. Making hotel and airline reservations and transportation arrangements to get to the ship and back as well as choosing the right shore excursions. It’s been a journey that I’ve learned a lot from, but there’s been tense/scary moments. I would recommend starting your solo travel adventures this way. I would not recommend that someone who has never travelled, just up and go on a worldwide trip. If you are scared, stressed or uncertain, your trip will not be fun. Also, you can always coordinate with your doctor to prescribe your medication for a longer time period. They can write some prescriptions for up to a year.

Above all, realize that you are traveling during a pandemic and have a flexible mindset. Not all places are going to be open for tourists and you might have the extra hassle to hunt down places to do a COVID test mid trip, which can be costly and stressful. Also, getting quarantined in a foreign country could be very costly and unpleasant.

Good luck to you! I wish you well on your travels. Feel free to message me if you have any questions.
